messages:
sanjay: Heads up — noticed a bunch of tenants hitting the rerank endpoint burst caps this morning. Console shows repeated 429s even though their committed quota should allow short bursts. Anyone digging into merged ratecap logic?
erica: I started a quick audit. It looks like when we merge per-tenant + per-route caps we apply the strictest window instead of additive burst windows. probably why short spikes are getting dropped. :thinking_face:
liz: @sanjay can you paste the example tenant id? I want to check routing + model affinity.
sanjay: tenant_42 — they fanout to 3 models for rescoring (v1, v1-quant, v2-lite). each candidate set is ~40, but the console shows fanout = 3 and request_units = 120 which is expected. the 429s happen in 10s spike windows.
erica: here's the relevant snippet from merging code: 
```
# in quota/merge.py
def merge_ratecaps(per_route, per_tenant):
    return min(per_route.window, per_tenant.window), min(per_route.capacity, per_tenant.capacity)
```
so we were returning min across dimensions which collapses burst window.
ops-bot: deploy/6912 finished to staging (quota-merge-fix).
mike: oof. that min() feels like a bad carryover from a previous simpler model. We need semantics: merged capacity should be min(capacities) but burst_window should be max(window) so tenant short-bursts are preserved. otherwise tenant-level permissive windows are negated.
tara: Agree. But console UX also confuses ops: it shows a single "effective_ratecap" and a timeline, no breakdown of why we enforced that window. We should surface both "applied_window_reason" and contributing caps.
liz: Also need to consider model-affinity hedging: some requests get dropped to single-model fallback and that affects observed fanout. Telemetry should tag which model variants were routed.
sanjay: Proposed change: merge logic -> (effective_capacity = min(capacities), effective_window = max(windows)). Also add contributing_caps array to response metadata: e.g. ["tenant:50r/10s","route:30r/1s","model:v2:40r/5s"] so console can explain.
erica: I like that. Minimal server-side change. But think about quota accounting: if window increases we might allow more short-term throughput that exceeds route-level intended smoothing. Does that break SLA?
mike: We should keep capacity enforcement per-slice: when we compute allowed_tokens in a tick, we apply effective_capacity with effective_window but still respect per-route token budget over rolling minute for SLA. In other words, allow tenant bursts but throttle if route long-window budget exceeded.
tara: UX: console will add a hover explaining "merged ratecap computed by min(capacity) + max(window) to preserve tenant burst windows while preventing capacity spikes beyond tightest cap over longer period." And show contributing_caps as pill chips.
liz: For telemetry we need a new tag: rerank.ratecap.applied=[tenant_min,route_min,model_v2] and rerank.routing.affinity=[v1:0.6,v2:0.3,quant:0.1]. That will help cost and regressions.
sanjay: Can we also emit a one-off audit event when effective_window != per_route.window so console can warn ops tenants may get unexpected burst len?
erica: yes, emit event type ratecap_audit with fields: tenant, route, contributing_caps, applied_window, applied_capacity, timestamp. keep it low-sampled.
mike: Dev note: update unit tests for quota/merge, add an integ test simulating 3-model fanout with short spikes. Also update docs in /internal/quotas.md.
tara: I'll mock up the console change (hover copy and contributing pill design) and drop a screenshot in #design later.
sanjay: plan sounds good. who wants the PR? I can take quota fix + tests. @erica you can add telemetry and audit event. @tara + @liz handle console + routing-affinity tags.
erica: assigned. I'll open PR by EOD.
liz: I'll coordinate with infra to run the integ test on staging after deploy.
sanjay: thanks all — goal: deploy patch, validate reduced 429s for tenant_42, and ship console affordance next week. :thumbsup:
